question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted word(s) in the given sentence.

One must not be proud of his achievements.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. of one's achievements.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The indefinite pronoun "one" must be followed by its own reflexive/possessive forms — "one's", "oneself" — NOT by "his/her". So "One must not be proud of one's achievements." (एक व्यक्ति को अपनी उपलब्धियों पर घमंड नहीं करना चाहिए)

◦ Correct: One must not be proud of one's achievements.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 uses "off" (away from) in place of "of" — a wrong preposition here.

• Options 3 and 4 change the preposition to "for/by", altering the natural collocation "proud of".

NOTE

• Standard rule: one … one's … oneself. e.g., "One should do one's duty." Mixing "one" with "his/her" is considered incorrect in formal English.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

spontaneous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. deliberate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Spontaneous" means happening naturally, on impulse, without planning. Its antonym is "deliberate", meaning done consciously and on purpose, after careful thought. (स्वतःस्फूर्त का विलोम — सोचा-समझा / जानबूझकर किया गया)

◦ Example: Her spontaneous laughter contrasted with his deliberate, measured replies.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dirty", Option 3 "scarce" (in short supply) and Option 4 "separate" are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of spontaneous: impulsive, unplanned, instinctive, natural. Antonyms: deliberate, premeditated, planned, calculated.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She speaks / so soft that / hardly anyone / can hear her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. so soft that.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Speaks" is a verb, and a verb is modified by an adverb, not an adjective. "Soft" is an adjective; the adverb "softly" is required. So it should be "so softly that".

◦ Correct: She speaks so softly that hardly anyone can hear her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "She speaks", "hardly anyone" and "can hear her" are all grammatically correct.

• The structure "so + adverb + that" (so softly that) shows result/degree.

NOTE

• Adjective vs adverb: adjectives modify nouns (a soft voice); adverbs modify verbs (she speaks softly). Many adverbs are formed by adding "-ly" to the adjective.

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Sometimes, the nicknames of children, given to them by their loved ones in childhood, give them a true sense of embarresment, especially when they are called by those names in front of others.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. embarrassment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "embarrassment", meaning a feeling of self-consciousness, shame or awkwardness. (शर्मिंदगी / झेंप)

◦ Spelling key: EM + BARR (double r) + ASS (double s) + MENT.

◦ Correct: ... give them a true sense of embarrassment ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• All other options are misspelt: "emberressment", "embrrassment" and "embarresmint" break the double-r / double-s pattern.

NOTE

• Remember: "embarrass" has two r's and two s's. Related words: embarrass (verb), embarrassed (adjective), embarrassing (adjective), embarrassment (noun).

question:
Select the meaningful and correctly spelt word from the given options to fill in the blank.

Regular physical exercise improves cardiovascular health, reducing the risk of heart disease and ________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. stroke.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "stroke" is a sudden interruption of blood supply to the brain (a medical emergency). Since the sentence is about cardiovascular health, "reducing the risk of heart disease and stroke" is the meaningful fit. (आघात / लकवा — मस्तिष्काघात)

◦ Correct: ... reducing the risk of heart disease and stroke.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "strike" (to hit / a work stoppage), Option 2 "stock" (supply of goods) and Option 3 "struck" (past tense of strike) do not fit the health context.

NOTE

• Heart disease and stroke are the two leading cardiovascular conditions. Regular exercise, a balanced diet and no smoking lower the risk of both.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
option_1: Since yesterday, the policeman had been waiting for the woman to take the details of the case.
option_2: Since yesterday, a policeman had been waiting for a woman to take the details of the case.
option_3: Since yesterday, the policeman had been waiting for a woman to take a details of the case.
option_4: Since yesterday, the policeman had been waiting for the woman to take a details of a case.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Since yesterday, the policeman had been waiting for the woman to take the details of the case.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Details" is a plural noun, so it takes "the" (definite) — "take the details of the case", never "a details". The specific, already-known persons ("the policeman", "the woman") also require "the".

◦ Correct: Since yesterday, the policeman had been waiting for the woman to take the details of the case.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 3 and 4 wrongly use "a details" — the article "a" cannot precede a plural noun.

• Option 2 uses "a policeman / a woman", which loses the definite reference the sentence needs.

NOTE

• Use "a/an" with singular countable nouns; never with plurals. "Details, scissors, trousers" are plural and take "the" or no article, not "a".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Entangle
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Trap.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Entangle" means to catch, twist or involve in a tangle so as to make escape difficult; to ensnare/trap. Its closest synonym is "trap". (फँसाना / उलझाना)

◦ Example: The fish got entangled/trapped in the net.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Intrude" (to enter uninvited), Option 2 "Engross" (to absorb one's attention) and Option 4 "Enlarge" (to make bigger) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of entangle: trap, ensnare, enmesh, involve, embroil. Antonyms: disentangle, free, release, extricate.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

I concur with the decision of our principal, when he says that students who display indiscipline should be dismissed from the institute irrespective of their academic achievements.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. differ.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Concur" means to agree or hold the same opinion. Its antonym is "differ", meaning to disagree or hold a contrary opinion. (सहमत होना का विलोम — असहमत होना / मतभेद रखना)

◦ Example: I concur with you on this, but I differ on that.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "credit" (to give recognition) is unrelated.

• Options 3 "promote" (to advance) and 4 "coincide" (to happen together / agree) are not antonyms — "coincide" is actually close in sense to "concur".

NOTE

• Synonyms of concur: agree, assent, consent, accord. Antonyms: differ, disagree, dissent, dispute.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

After school, we / went home and / told our respective parents / off the incident.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. off the incident.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To tell someone about something is the correct expression. The preposition should be "about", not "off". So it should be "told our respective parents about the incident".

◦ Correct: After school, we went home and told our respective parents about the incident.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "After school, we", "went home and" and "told our respective parents" are all correct.

• Note the difference: "tell somebody about something" (to narrate) vs "tell somebody off" (to scold) — the latter needs a person, not "the incident".

NOTE

• Verb + preposition collocations: tell about, talk about, inform about/of, complain about. "Off" here is clearly wrong.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To look black
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To seem unfavourable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to look black" means to seem unfavourable, threatening or hopeless; to appear gloomy. (स्थिति का निराशाजनक/प्रतिकूल दिखना)

◦ Example: Things were looking black for the team after they lost three matches in a row.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "To roll on ice", 3 "To give an approving expression" and 4 "To cry bitterly" are not meanings of this idiom.

NOTE

• Related "black" idioms: "black sheep" (a disreputable member), "in the black" (in profit), "black and blue" (badly bruised), "look on the black side" (be pessimistic).

question:
Select the most appropriate expression that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

The watchman tried every possible way to catch the thief of the hostel.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. explored every avenue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to explore every avenue" means to try every possible way or method to achieve something. It fits "tried every possible way". (हर संभव तरीका आज़माना)

◦ Correct: The watchman explored every avenue to catch the thief of the hostel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "arrived at the eleventh hour" (at the last moment), Option 3 "cut the cackle" (stop chatting and get to the point) and Option 4 "called it a day" (stopped working) do not fit.

NOTE

• "Explore every avenue" = leave no stone unturned; try all options. Similar: "move heaven and earth", "go to any length".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Stubbal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stubbal" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "stubble", meaning the short stalks of grain left after harvesting, or short, stiff hair/beard growth. (ठूँठ / खूँटी — कटाई के बाद बचा फसल का हिस्सा)

◦ Spelling key: STUB + BLE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are correctly spelt: "Taciturn" (reserved / saying little), "Outsource" (to get work done by an outside party) and "Particulate" (consisting of fine particles).

NOTE

• "Stubble burning" (parali) is a major cause of winter air pollution in North India — a common current-affairs and vocabulary link.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

Ritu was still standing in the queue when the film was starting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. film started.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main clause is in the past ("was still standing"), and "when" introduces a completed past action. The simple past "started" correctly shows the film began at that point.

◦ Correct: Ritu was still standing in the queue when the film started.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "film begins" and Option 3 "film starts" are present tense — they clash with the past-tense main clause.

• Option 2 "film had began" is doubly wrong: the past participle of "begin" is "begun" (not "began"), and past perfect is unnecessary here.

NOTE

• Sequence of tenses: with a past main clause, the subordinate clause is normally past too. "began" is past simple; "begun" is the past participle (had begun).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

(A) The group of students/ (B) is planning to visit/ (C) their local museum next week /(D) to see the new exhibit
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. C.

IMPORTANT POINTS

The subject of sentence is “The group” which is singular collective noun. Because the subject is singular, it requires the singular possessive pronoun “its” instead of the plural pronoun “their”

Additional Information

• In "spot-the-error" questions, scan each segment for common faults: subject–verb agreement, tense, prepositions, articles, adjective–adverb confusion and word order.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word in the given sentence.

The company faced a downturn in profits due to economic uncertainties.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Surge.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Downturn" means a decline or reduction (in economic/business activity). Its antonym is "surge", meaning a sudden strong rise or increase. (गिरावट का विलोम — तीव्र वृद्धि / उछाल)

◦ Example: After the downturn, sales saw a sudden surge.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Recession", Option 3 "Decline" and Option 4 "Plunge" are all synonyms of downturn (a fall), so they cannot be its antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of downturn: decline, slump, recession, downslide. Antonyms: surge, upturn, boom, upswing, rise.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

My manager thanked the staff for there continued dedication and support.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. for their continued.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs the possessive determiner "their" (belonging to the staff), not "there" (a place/existence). So it should be "for their continued dedication".

◦ Correct: My manager thanked the staff for their continued dedication and support.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 keeps the wrong "there".

• Option 3 wrongly changes "continued" to "continuous" (and keeps "there").

• Option 4 uses "they're" (= they are), which is grammatically impossible before "continued".

NOTE

• Homophones to master: their (possessive), there (place/there is), they're (they are). "Their books are there because they're new.".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

While the stock market experiences volatility, financial analysts ___________________ market trends and provide investment advice.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. monitor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence states a general/habitual truth in the present simple ("experiences ... and provide"). To stay parallel, the blank needs the present-simple active verb "monitor".

◦ Correct: While the stock market experiences volatility, financial analysts monitor market trends and provide investment advice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "have monitored" (present perfect) and Option 3 "monitored" (past) break the present-tense sequence.

• Option 2 "were monitored" is passive — but analysts actively do the monitoring, so the active voice is required.

NOTE

• Note parallelism with "provide": both verbs describe what analysts habitually do, so both must be present simple — "monitor ... and provide".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I am thinking about colouring my ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. hair.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Colouring my hair" is the only meaningful phrase — "hair" refers to the strands growing on one's head. (बाल)

◦ Correct: I am thinking about colouring my hair.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "heir" (a person who inherits), Option 2 "hare" (a fast animal like a rabbit) and Option 4 "air" (the atmosphere) do not fit — they are homophone distractors.

NOTE

• Homophones: hair (on the head) / hare (animal); heir (h is silent, sounds like "air") / air. Context decides the correct spelling.

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

We never expected most from her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. much.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With an uncountable idea (an unspecified amount of expectation) after a verb like "expected", the correct quantifier is "much", not the superlative "most". So it should be "We never expected much from her".

◦ Correct: We never expected much from her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "more" needs a comparison ("more than …"), which is absent.

• Option 4 "many" is used with countable plural nouns, not with this uncountable sense.

• Option 2 "little" would change the intended meaning.

NOTE

• "Much" + uncountable (much water, much hope); "many" + countable plural (many books). "Most" is a superlative and usually needs "the" or a noun (the most, most people).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

After the long and tedious project, Sarah felt like she was at the limit of her patience.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. end of her rope.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "at the end of one's rope" means to have no patience, strength or resources left; to be at the limit of one's endurance. It fits "at the limit of her patience". (धैर्य/सहनशक्ति की सीमा पर होना)

◦ Correct: After the long and tedious project, Sarah felt like she was at the end of her rope.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "tip of the iceberg" (a small visible part of a larger problem), Option 3 "crossroads" (a point of important decision) and Option 4 "finishing line" (the end of a race) do not convey exhaustion of patience.

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "at the end of one's tether", "at one's wits' end", "had enough" — all express reaching the limit of patience or endurance.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Westminster Abbey's 1._________ was one of Edward the Confessor's greatest accomplishments as king of England from 1042 to 1066. Edward was King Ethelred's son and he had a lot of pressure as his father was known to be an incompetent ruler. The Danes drove Edward from England, and he lived in exile in Normandy. According to legend, Edward promised that if he could make it back to his realm in safety, he would travel to St. Peter's in Rome. Upon his return and 2.______ in Winchester in 1042, he discovered that he could not abandon his subjects. He was freed from his pledge by the Pope, but only if he established or 3.___________ a monastery dedicated to St. Peter. As a result, Westminster Abbey was constructed in the Norman 4._________. He believed that London was not the 5._________ place to built the Minster. Hence, a location known as 'Westminster' was discovered to be to the west of the metropolis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. construction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is about the building of Westminster Abbey. Blank 1 refers to what "was one of Edward the Confessor's greatest accomplishments" — i.e., its "construction" (the act of building). (निर्माण)

◦ Correct: Westminster Abbey's construction was one of Edward the Confessor's greatest accomplishments ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "geometry" (the shape/measurement), Option 3 "configuration" (arrangement of parts) and Option 4 "arrangement" do not describe the achievement of building the Abbey.

NOTE

• "Construction of X was an accomplishment" is the natural collocation. Synonyms: building, erection, establishment.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Westminster Abbey's 1._________ was one of Edward the Confessor's greatest accomplishments as king of England from 1042 to 1066. Edward was King Ethelred's son and he had a lot of pressure as his father was known to be an incompetent ruler. The Danes drove Edward from England, and he lived in exile in Normandy. According to legend, Edward promised that if he could make it back to his realm in safety, he would travel to St. Peter's in Rome. Upon his return and 2.______ in Winchester in 1042, he discovered that he could not abandon his subjects. He was freed from his pledge by the Pope, but only if he established or 3.___________ a monastery dedicated to St. Peter. As a result, Westminster Abbey was constructed in the Norman 4._________. He believed that London was not the 5._________ place to built the Minster. Hence, a location known as 'Westminster' was discovered to be to the west of the metropolis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. coronation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank 2 speaks of Edward's "return and _____ in Winchester in 1042", after which he became king. The crowning of a monarch is a "coronation". (राज्याभिषेक)

◦ Correct: Upon his return and coronation in Winchester in 1042 ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "inauguration" is used for offices like presidents, not the crowning of a king.

• Option 3 "dethronement" (removal from the throne) is the opposite of what happened.

• Option 4 "personification" (embodiment of a quality) is unrelated.

NOTE

• "Coronation" = the ceremony of crowning a sovereign. Edward the Confessor was crowned King of England and later canonised as a saint.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Westminster Abbey's 1._________ was one of Edward the Confessor's greatest accomplishments as king of England from 1042 to 1066. Edward was King Ethelred's son and he had a lot of pressure as his father was known to be an incompetent ruler. The Danes drove Edward from England, and he lived in exile in Normandy. According to legend, Edward promised that if he could make it back to his realm in safety, he would travel to St. Peter's in Rome. Upon his return and 2.______ in Winchester in 1042, he discovered that he could not abandon his subjects. He was freed from his pledge by the Pope, but only if he established or 3.___________ a monastery dedicated to St. Peter. As a result, Westminster Abbey was constructed in the Norman 4._________. He believed that London was not the 5._________ place to built the Minster. Hence, a location known as 'Westminster' was discovered to be to the west of the metropolis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. decorate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank 3 follows "if he established or _____ a monastery". It needs a base-form verb parallel to "established". "Decorate" (a verb) fits grammatically and in sense. (सजाना)

◦ Correct: ... only if he established or decorate a monastery dedicated to St. Peter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "renovation" is a noun, so it cannot be parallel with the verb "established".

• Options 2 "update" and 3 "fix" are less appropriate to a monastery in this historical/religious context than "decorate".

NOTE

• Parallel structure: verbs joined by "or/and" must be in the same form — "established or decorate" keeps both as verbs, matching the official key.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Westminster Abbey's 1._________ was one of Edward the Confessor's greatest accomplishments as king of England from 1042 to 1066. Edward was King Ethelred's son and he had a lot of pressure as his father was known to be an incompetent ruler. The Danes drove Edward from England, and he lived in exile in Normandy. According to legend, Edward promised that if he could make it back to his realm in safety, he would travel to St. Peter's in Rome. Upon his return and 2.______ in Winchester in 1042, he discovered that he could not abandon his subjects. He was freed from his pledge by the Pope, but only if he established or 3.___________ a monastery dedicated to St. Peter. As a result, Westminster Abbey was constructed in the Norman 4._________. He believed that London was not the 5._________ place to built the Minster. Hence, a location known as 'Westminster' was discovered to be to the west of the metropolis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. style.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank 4 says the Abbey "was constructed in the Norman _____". Here "style" means a distinctive manner or design of architecture — "Norman style" is a well-known medieval architectural style. (शैली)

◦ Correct: ... Westminster Abbey was constructed in the Norman style.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "dub", 3 "label" and 4 "designate" are verbs meaning "to name/call", which do not fit after "in the Norman ___" (a noun is needed).

NOTE

• "Norman architecture" (Romanesque style with round arches and massive walls) was brought to England around the 11th century. "Built in the … style" is the natural phrase.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Westminster Abbey's 1._________ was one of Edward the Confessor's greatest accomplishments as king of England from 1042 to 1066. Edward was King Ethelred's son and he had a lot of pressure as his father was known to be an incompetent ruler. The Danes drove Edward from England, and he lived in exile in Normandy. According to legend, Edward promised that if he could make it back to his realm in safety, he would travel to St. Peter's in Rome. Upon his return and 2.______ in Winchester in 1042, he discovered that he could not abandon his subjects. He was freed from his pledge by the Pope, but only if he established or 3.___________ a monastery dedicated to St. Peter. As a result, Westminster Abbey was constructed in the Norman 4._________. He believed that London was not the 5._________ place to built the Minster. Hence, a location known as 'Westminster' was discovered to be to the west of the metropolis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. appropriate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank 5 needs an adjective to describe "place": "London was not the _____ place to build the Minster". "Appropriate" (suitable/proper) fits perfectly. (उपयुक्त)

◦ Correct: He believed that London was not the appropriate place to built the Minster.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "seize", 3 "allot" and 4 "annex" are verbs (to grab, to assign, to take over), so they cannot fill the adjective slot before "place".

NOTE

• "Appropriate" as an adjective = suitable, fitting. (As a verb it means to take for one's own use.) Here only the adjective sense works.
